title: Inquest to be ordered in P.A. police shooting
article: Prince Albert police shot a man three times in a confrontation that left a 27-yearold dead last month, the man's grandfather says.
"It's a sad thing to say what happened," Christian Nelson said of the July 9 incident that left Ryan Natomagan-Nelson dead.
"Two police going after one little guy."
A Ministry of Justice spokesperson said there will be a coroner's inquest into Natomagan-Nelson's death, but no date has been set for the hearing.

Last month, Prince Albert police reported that two officers, responding to a domestic dispute with a report that a woman had been assaulted, shot the man at a housing complex in the city's east side when he confronted officers with a knife.
After the shooting, paramedics took Natomagan-Nelson to Victoria Hospital in Prince Albert, where he was pronounced dead.
Nelson said his grandson was not a large man.
"They shot him three times without ever going after him. That's why I don't like it," he said.

Someone has posted a 16-minute video on YouTube, titled In Loving Memory of Ryan Natomagan-Nelson, featuring dozens of family pictures, from a toddler sitting on a dock at a lake, to a shirt-and-tie-wearing little boy sitting on Santa's knee, to a young man dressed up next to his date, presumably for a high-school graduation.
Relatives contacted by The StarPhoenix were reluctant to talk about the young man, who is originally from the northern hamlet of Weyakwin.

Two investigations into Natomagan-Nelson's death, including a review of the police use of force, are currently underway - one by Prince Albert city police themselves, and another by an overseer appointed by the deputy minister of justice, ministry spokesperson Janice Wilby said.

The independent investigator - whose identity the ministry refuses to disclose - can independently interview witnesses, and will evaluate the adequacy of the police investigation, then provide a confidential report to the deputy minister of justice, Wilby said. Wilby said she does not know when either investigation might be complete. Repeated calls seeking comment from Prince Albert police over the past week were not successful.
It's not known whether the officers involved in the July shooting were carrying conducted energy weapons, known as Tasers.

In January, after five years of study, the Saskatchewan Police Commission cleared the way for all municipal police officers to carry CEWs. News reports from Prince Albert in January said the force intended to purchase the devices and train members on their use. At the time, police did not give a timeline for when officers might be carrying the devices.
